title: Differential concurrency pools & latency‑tiered billing (per-route entitlements and graceful overage)
creator: Maya Thompson
description: PRD to introduce differential concurrency pools (per-plan / per-route concurrency entitlements) and a latency‑aware billing fallback that gracefully throttles and applies overage accounting when committed capacity is exhausted. Goal is to give enterprise customers predictable concurrency guarantees while enabling soft overage behavior that prioritizes low-latency traffic and transparently bills excess usage.
background: Customers on Dedicated and large Hosted plans ask for more predictable concurrency guarantees per product route (embedding vs. generation) and clearer behavioral contracts when usage exceeds reserved capacity. Current single-queue concurrency model leads to noisy neighbor effects and heavy tail latency spikes. Billing teams require deterministic events for invoicing overage. This PRD defines entitlements (concurrency pools), soft-throttle policies by latency tier, and billing triggers for overage and emergency burst credits.
goals: Define per-plan concurrency pools that can be assigned to routes or route groups
Implement latency-tiered soft-throttling rules that prioritize requests under configured SLOs
Surface clear billing events (metered records) when overage occurs and capture pre/post SLO metrics for invoicing
Provide admin UI + API for customers to map routes to pools and review projected overage costs
non_goals: This phase does not change per-token pricing or model-level compute credit rates
We will not support cross-tenant quota pooling in this iteration
No changes to existing authentication or billing accounts; entitlement mapping is per existing account ID
stakeholders: Eng leads: Priya Patel (runtime), Aaron Chen (billing infra)
requirements: R1: Concurrency Pool API - create/update/delete pools with fields: name, concurrency_limit, allowed_routes (list of route IDs), priority_tier (0 high / 1 normal / 2 low)
R2: Route binding - allow customers and admins to bind a route to a pool via Console and REST API
R3: Enforcement - runtime must enforce per-pool concurrency limits and preempt lower priority requests when capacity is constrained

R4: Latency-tiered soft-throttle - when capacity exceeds threshold, accept requests but mark them as 'soft-throttled' if expected latency > configured Tier threshold; map soft-throttled requests to overage billing if they consume reserve capacity
R5: Billing events - emit metered overage records with fields: timestamp, account_id, pool_id, route_id, request_id, latency_bucket, tokens_consumed
R6: Predictive estimator - Console shows 7-day projected overage cost given current traffic and pool assignments
R7: Audit logs - every pool change (create/update/delete/binding) must be recorded with actor, timestamp, and prior state
R8: Fallback behavior - if billing export fails, queries must persist metering locally and retry; do not drop metering records
edge_cases: EC1: Two pools share the same physical worker; enforcement must be coordinated to avoid double-counting concurrency limits
EC2: Burst traffic that momentarily spikes above concurrency_limit — define emergency burst window (configurable, default 30s) where requests are allowed but flagged for overage if sustained
EC3: Partially bound routes - route A bound to pool X but has active long-running generation calls; new requests should respect pool limits and latency tiers
EC4: Cross-region failover - if region fallback routes are used, overage billing must be attributed to original account and pool
EC5: Meter duplication - ensure dedup keys on metering export for retries to avoid double billing
milestone_checklist: 1) API design review completed (Confluence doc + OpenAPI) - done
3) Billing export pipeline & schema - QA ready
4) Console UI for pool management + estimator - design mock approved
5) End-to-end E2E test matrix and chaos tests - ready
6) Pilot with 3 customers and billing reconciliation - planned
7) GA rollout and billing enablement - gated on successful pilot
rollout_plan: Alpha (internal): feature-flagged for Redwood internal accounts only. Validate enforcement and metering for 1 week
Beta (partners): enable for two existing enterprise customers (opt-in). Collect reconciliation feedback and UI usability inputs
Pilot (selected customers): 3 customers across Hosted and Dedicated; run for 30 days with weekly reconciliation meetings
GA: default available to all customers; existing customers must opt in to create pools; updated billing docs published
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A customer can create a concurrency pool via API and bind an existing route; binding is reflected in Console within 30s
AC-2: Under synthetic test load, pool concurrency_limit is enforced across 95th percentile of requests; no pool exceeds its limit without being flagged for emergency burst
AC-3: Soft-throttled requests are recorded and surfaced in billing exports with correct latency_bucket and tokens_consumed fields
AC-4: Console estimator shows projected overage within ±15% of measured overage during 7-day test window
AC-5: Billing export pipeline successfully ingests metered records for 99.9% of events in a 24-hour run; failures are retried without duplication
AC-6: Pilot customers sign off (Customer Success + Revenue Ops) on accuracy of metering for at least two weeks of pilot data
AC-7: No regressions in existing per-token invoice totals for accounts not using pools (regression test pass)
analytics_metrics: Metric: pool_enforced_rate (percent of requests correctly counted against pool limits)
Metric: customer_complaints_re. overage (tracked in Zendesk tags)
